messages.subject: Adding ListDataListener to VariableListWidget
parts:
I'm working on a package that includes a preview screen and I would like the preview to refresh each time there is a change in the variables in a VariableListWidget (that's the widget that the variables move INTO).  I'm working in Java because there is no preview widget yet.  All the selections that would trigger the change are in a SimpleRSubdialog called "Options".  Here's the beginning:

public class WideToLong2 extends RDialog implements KeyListener, ActionListener, ListSelectionListener, ListDataListener {
...
Options = new SimpleRSubDialog(this,"Options");
...
optionDataSelector = new VariableSelectorWidget();
...
DropVariables = new VariableListWidget("Variables to Drop",optionDataSelector);

I would like to add a ListDataListener to DropVariables so that whenever the variables in that VariableListWidget change, the preview updates.  The addListener method for VariableListWidget has different effects depending on the type of EventListener that is assigned, but none of these are ListDataListeners:

    public void addListener(EventListener lis) {
        if(lis instanceof ActionListener){
            removeButton.addActionListener((ActionListener) lis);
            addButton.addActionListener((ActionListener) lis);
        }
        if(lis instanceof ListSelectionListener)
            varList.addListSelectionListener((ListSelectionListener) lis);
        if(lis instanceof MouseListener)
            varList.addMouseListener((MouseListener) lis);

I thought I could extract the model from DropVariables and then assign a listener to that.  The getModel method for VariableListWidget is:

public Object getModel() {
        return varList.getModel();
    }

where varList is defined as a DJList, which extends JList and has DefaultListModel as its model.  To get to it:

DefaultListModel dropModel = (DefaultListModel)DropVariables.getModel();
dropModel.addListDataListener(new LDListener());

where LDListener is a class implementing ListDataListener.

Unfortunately, that doesn't work.  Attaching a listener to the add or remove buttons doesn't work either, because the listener fires before those buttons have their effects on changing the model.  Does anyone have suggestions on how to listen for changes to the DefaultListModel model of a VariableListWidget?

Thanks,
--Bill
